$releaseOnlyComment: Engine-internal release tooling. Overrides engineOwnedPaths (which globs scripts/**): these paths are NEVER distributed to formulacms-starter nor synced to forks — the slice ship-list + report command that curate which slices ship. Their presence is also the engine-vs-starter signal for the /admin/slices 'Ship to starter' toggle, so shipping them would surface engine-only tooling in a fork.
$pathsComment: engineOwnedPaths: expect these to fast-forward from upstream on sync; local edits there are upstream-port candidates (playbook step 10). ownerOwnedPaths: the site owner's own surface (slice descriptors and renderers the owner authored, design tokens, assets). On a merge conflict there, keep the owner's version; upstream changes that do not conflict may still merge in silently, so review them. lib/slices/slices.manifest.json stays listed here for the admin design-system drift report; on an upgrade its sharedRegistries class wins. The exact convex/lib/slices/*.ts entries in engineOwnedPaths are engine files inside the owner-owned slice folder. releaseOnlyPaths takes precedence over engineOwnedPaths: a path it matches is engine-local and excluded from distribution even when an engineOwnedPaths glob (e.g. scripts/**) also matches it.
$classesComment: Upgrade merge classes. When a path matches more than one class, the first match in this order wins: releaseOnlyPaths > sharedRegistries (manifest, then generated files) > pathRules > an exact-path entry in any list > an ownerOwnedPaths glob > an engineOwnedPaths glob > defaultRule. The formulacms release tooling classifies paths in this same order.

sharedRegistries.rule: Keep both sides' entries in the manifest. Never edit the generated files by hand: take either side, then run the regenerate command and confirm the check command passes.
Keep both sides' entries in the manifest. Never edit the generated files by hand: take either side, then run the regenerate command and confirm the check command passes.

pathRules.rule: Keep both sides' dependency and script entries, one entry at a time. Never keep a whole conflicting block from one side. When one package changed on both sides, take the starter's version unless you pinned yours on purpose.

Never edit it by hand. Resolve package.json first. Then take the starter's lockfile (git checkout --theirs pnpm-lock.yaml), or leave the conflict markers in, because pnpm removes them. Run pnpm install. Then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile must pass.
Resolve each conflict on its own. Keep your text and styling, and keep the starter's new keys and fixes. Never take a whole file from one side.

defaultRule: Resolve each conflict on its own. Keep your text and styling, and keep the starter's new keys and fixes. Never take a whole file from one side.
